title: Guaranteed and Viable Curriculum
summary: Shared grade/course expectations cover all required standards, with time for teaching, practice, review and support.
criteria: Teachers use a **shared curriculum aligned to all required Kentucky Academic Standards**. Priority Standards focus essential learning without excluding other required standards. Teams plan **sufficient time for instruction, practice, review and additional support** across classrooms and schools.
description: Accountability measure: percentage of reviewed **grade/course curriculum sequences** meeting the expectation below. Teachers use a **shared curriculum aligned to all required Kentucky Academic Standards**. Priority Standards focus essential learning without excluding other required standards. Teams plan **sufficient time for instruction, practice, review and additional support** across classrooms and schools.
evidence: Curriculum and pacing records; aligned tasks and assessments; annotated examples; student explanations. For standards and scale measures, count one student/Priority Standard pair per review period and record the applicable timing.
why: Families can count on consistent learning expectations across schools, and students have the time they need to meet them.

title: Kentucky Priority Standards: Learning and Purpose
summary: At the introduction of each Priority Standard, students explain WHAT they are learning, WHY it matters and its use.
criteria: At the start of instruction on each Priority Standard, teachers establish the learning and its purpose. Students explain **WHAT they are learning, WHY it matters and where they can use it**, in their own words, and connect their work to that purpose.
description: Accountability measure: percentage of reviewed **student-standard opportunities** meeting the expectation below. At the start of instruction on each Priority Standard, teachers establish the learning and its purpose. Students explain **WHAT they are learning, WHY it matters and where they can use it**, in their own words, and connect their work to that purpose.
evidence: Curriculum and pacing records; aligned tasks and assessments; annotated examples; student explanations. For standards and scale measures, count one student/Priority Standard pair per review period and record the applicable timing.
why: Students can see a purpose for today's work and understand where they might use what they are learning.

title: Proficiency Scales: Exemplar Review and Discussion
summary: Before first demonstrating proficiency, students compare examples with the aligned scale and explain specific features of quality.
criteria: Before their first demonstration of proficiency on each Priority Standard with a scale, students **compare and discuss examples of different quality** using the aligned scale. They identify **specific features that meet the criteria** and explain what to apply in their own work.
description: Accountability measure: percentage of reviewed **student-standard opportunities** meeting the expectation below. Before their first demonstration of proficiency on each Priority Standard with a scale, students **compare and discuss examples of different quality** using the aligned scale. They identify **specific features that meet the criteria** and explain what to apply in their own work.
evidence: Curriculum and pacing records; aligned tasks and assessments; annotated examples; student explanations. For standards and scale measures, count one student/Priority Standard pair per review period and record the applicable timing.
why: Studying examples makes what quality work looks like visible before students are expected to produce it themselves.

title: Grade-Level Expectations
summary: Students do the standard's grade-level thinking themselves, with accessible materials, scaffolds and required accommodations.
criteria: Tasks and assessments match the standard's **knowledge, skills and level of thinking**. Teachers provide accessible materials, models and scaffolds while maintaining the learning expectation. Students **explain their reasoning and do the thinking themselves**, with approved accommodations as needed.
description: Accountability measure: percentage of reviewed **student task opportunities** meeting the expectation below. Tasks and assessments match the standard's **knowledge, skills and level of thinking**. Teachers provide accessible materials, models and scaffolds while maintaining the learning expectation. Students **explain their reasoning and do the thinking themselves**, with approved accommodations as needed.
evidence: Curriculum and pacing records; aligned tasks and assessments; annotated examples; student explanations. For standards and scale measures, count one student/Priority Standard pair per review period and record the applicable timing.
why: Every student gets the opportunity to do the challenging work expected at their grade level.

title: Real-world Learning Connections
summary: Students apply grade-level knowledge to authentic problems, compare responses and justify decisions with evidence.
criteria: Students apply **grade-level knowledge and skills to an authentic problem, need or decision** connected to life, community or work. They explain who is affected, compare possible responses and **justify a solution or recommendation with evidence**.
description: Accountability measure: percentage of reviewed **student application tasks** meeting the expectation below. Students apply **grade-level knowledge and skills to an authentic problem, need or decision** connected to life, community or work. They explain who is affected, compare possible responses and **justify a solution or recommendation with evidence**.
evidence: Task designs, identified standards, student reasoning and products. For partner design, record the contributor, group, input, design change and date; assess student learning separately from partner participation.
why: Students learn to weigh evidence and make decisions they can explain when they face a real problem.

title: Interdisciplinary Learning
summary: Students integrate two or more disciplines in one task and explain each subject's contribution; relevant standards are assessed.
criteria: When a problem requires multiple subjects, students use **learning from two or more disciplines in one coherent task**. Teachers identify and assess the relevant standards in each discipline. Students explain **what each subject contributes** to their understanding or solution.
description: Accountability measure: percentage of reviewed **student interdisciplinary tasks** meeting the expectation below. When a problem requires multiple subjects, students use **learning from two or more disciplines in one coherent task**. Teachers identify and assess the relevant standards in each discipline. Students explain **what each subject contributes** to their understanding or solution.
evidence: Task designs, identified standards, student reasoning and products. For partner design, record the contributor, group, input, design change and date; assess student learning separately from partner participation.
why: Students see how learning from different classes works together when they face a problem outside the classroom.

title: Community Partnerships in Learning Design
summary: Family, community and workforce contributions shape learning design; records identify the input and what changed.
criteria: Teachers develop learning experiences **in partnership with families, community members and local workforce partners**. Partners help frame problems, contribute expertise or define authentic success criteria. Plans and student explanations show **how partner input shaped the learning**, with opportunities accessible to all students. Record each contributor group and its design contribution; audience attendance alone does not establish co-design. A single partnership finding does not establish all elements of a qualifying vibrant learning experience.
description: Accountability measure: percentage of reviewed **learning-design records** meeting the expectation below. Teachers develop learning experiences **in partnership with families, community members and local workforce partners**. Partners help frame problems, contribute expertise or define authentic success criteria. Plans and student explanations show **how partner input shaped the learning**, with opportunities accessible to all students. Record each contributor group and its design contribution; audience attendance alone does not establish co-design. A single partnership finding does not establish all elements of a qualifying vibrant learning experience.
evidence: Task designs, identified standards, student reasoning and products. For partner design, record the contributor, group, input, design change and date; assess student learning separately from partner participation.
why: Partners help students understand who faces the problem, what is at stake, and what a workable response would look like.

title: Student Voice
summary: Students identify a learning decision influenced by their input and explain what changed.
criteria: Students **influence learning decisions**. Teachers explain how student input was used, and students identify **what changed because of their input**. Evidence connects a student contribution to an actual decision about questions, learning experiences or classroom practice.
description: Accountability measure: percentage of reviewed **student learning experiences** meeting the expectation below. Students **influence learning decisions**. Teachers explain how student input was used, and students identify **what changed because of their input**. Evidence connects a student contribution to an actual decision about questions, learning experiences or classroom practice.
evidence: Student proposals, decision records, inquiry notes, work and student explanations showing the influence of input, meaningful choices and follow-up.
why: Students see that speaking up can influence decisions about how they learn.

title: Student Choice
summary: Students make consequential choices about learning and explain how their choices meet shared expectations.
criteria: Students make **meaningful choices about questions, approaches or demonstrations of learning**. They explain their reasons, how their choices shaped the work and **how the work meets shared learning expectations**.
description: Accountability measure: percentage of reviewed **student learning experiences** meeting the expectation below. Students make **meaningful choices about questions, approaches or demonstrations of learning**. They explain their reasons, how their choices shaped the work and **how the work meets shared learning expectations**.
evidence: Student proposals, decision records, inquiry notes, work and student explanations showing the influence of input, meaningful choices and follow-up.
why: Meaningful choices help students take responsibility for their work and think through the decisions they make.

title: Interests, Passions, Aspirations, Skills and Talents
summary: Students connect work to personal interests, strengths, experiences or aspirations and identify a further opportunity to explore.
criteria: Students connect a specific task, product or investigation to **their interests, passions, strengths, skills, talents, cultural knowledge, lived experiences or aspirations**. They explain how that connection shaped their work and identify **a further learning or career possibility** to explore.
description: Accountability measure: percentage of reviewed **student learning experiences** meeting the expectation below. Students connect a specific task, product or investigation to **their interests, passions, strengths, skills, talents, cultural knowledge, lived experiences or aspirations**. They explain how that connection shaped their work and identify **a further learning or career possibility** to explore.
evidence: Student proposals, decision records, inquiry notes, work and student explanations showing the influence of input, meaningful choices and follow-up.
why: Students see how who they are and what they care about can shape what they learn and what they might pursue.

title: Exploration and Discovery
summary: Students ask questions, investigate and test ideas, explain discoveries and identify what to explore next.
criteria: Students **generate questions, investigate ideas and test possibilities** using appropriate sources, tools or experiences. They examine evidence, revise an explanation or approach, and describe **what they discovered and what they want to investigate next**. Teachers provide time and guidance for this inquiry.
description: Accountability measure: percentage of reviewed **student inquiry cycles** meeting the expectation below. Students **generate questions, investigate ideas and test possibilities** using appropriate sources, tools or experiences. They examine evidence, revise an explanation or approach, and describe **what they discovered and what they want to investigate next**. Teachers provide time and guidance for this inquiry.
evidence: Student proposals, decision records, inquiry notes, work and student explanations showing the influence of input, meaningful choices and follow-up.
why: Makes exploration and discovery visible through evidence of practice and student learning.

title: Writing Across the Content
summary: Students write weekly in every course; teachers give feedback on subject thinking and relevant writing criteria.
criteria: Students **write weekly in every course** to explain reasoning, interpret evidence or communicate subject knowledge. Teachers give feedback on **thinking and relevant writing criteria**; dated samples show student-generated ideas.
description: Accountability measure: percentage of reviewed **student-course instructional weeks** meeting the expectation below. Students **write weekly in every course** to explain reasoning, interpret evidence or communicate subject knowledge. Teachers give feedback on **thinking and relevant writing criteria**; dated samples show student-generated ideas.
evidence: Dated student work, criteria shared before assessment, individual demonstrations, project milestones, BPI feedback, website reviews and presentation evidence. Record the district schedule for portfolios, websites and Presentations of Learning; weekly writing is measured separately.
why: Writing makes students' thinking visible and gives them practice communicating clearly in every subject.

title: Performance-based Assessments
summary: Students apply standards in authentic demonstrations; teachers assess each student with criteria shared in advance.
criteria: Students **apply standards through products, performances or explanations**. Teachers share criteria in advance, assess **each student's demonstrated learning** and give feedback. Completion alone does not establish proficiency.
description: Accountability measure: percentage of reviewed **individual performance-assessment records** meeting the expectation below. Students **apply standards through products, performances or explanations**. Teachers share criteria in advance, assess **each student's demonstrated learning** and give feedback. Completion alone does not establish proficiency.
evidence: Dated student work, criteria shared before assessment, individual demonstrations, project milestones, BPI feedback, website reviews and presentation evidence. Record the district schedule for portfolios, websites and Presentations of Learning; weekly writing is measured separately.
why: Evidence from more than one piece of work gives students, families, and teachers a clearer picture of what students can do with their learning.

title: BPI Portfolios and Presentations of Learning
unit: scheduled student portfolio/presentation cycles in grades 3-12
summary: In grades 3-12, students justify growth, mastery, readiness and BPI claims with portfolio evidence and answer audience questions.
criteria: In **grades 3-12**, students use selected portfolio evidence to explain **growth, mastery, readiness and BPI development**. They justify claims, answer audience questions and identify next steps. Teachers provide preparation, accessible participation and feedback that students use to refine goals. Students select relevant BPI portfolio artifacts and explain what each demonstrates; record the district's presentation schedule.
description: Accountability measure: percentage of reviewed **scheduled student portfolio/presentation cycles in grades 3-12** meeting the expectation below. In **grades 3-12**, students use selected portfolio evidence to explain **growth, mastery, readiness and BPI development**. They justify claims, answer audience questions and identify next steps. Teachers provide preparation, accessible participation and feedback that students use to refine goals. Students select relevant BPI portfolio artifacts and explain what each demonstrates; record the district's presentation schedule.
evidence: Dated student work, criteria shared before assessment, individual demonstrations, project milestones, BPI feedback, website reviews and presentation evidence. Record the district schedule for portfolios, websites and Presentations of Learning; weekly writing is measured separately.
why: Students learn to explain their progress using evidence they selected and can discuss with others.

title: Project-Based Learning
summary: Sustained inquiry includes standards, decisions, critique, revision, an appropriate audience and checks of individual learning.
criteria: Students learn through **sustained inquiry into a meaningful question or challenge**. They apply standards, make decisions, use feedback and revision, and share a product or response with **an audience connected to its purpose**. Teachers check individual learning at project milestones.
description: Accountability measure: percentage of reviewed **student project cycles** meeting the expectation below. Students learn through **sustained inquiry into a meaningful question or challenge**. They apply standards, make decisions, use feedback and revision, and share a product or response with **an audience connected to its purpose**. Teachers check individual learning at project milestones.
evidence: Dated student work, criteria shared before assessment, individual demonstrations, project milestones, BPI feedback, website reviews and presentation evidence. Record the district schedule for portfolios, websites and Presentations of Learning; weekly writing is measured separately.
why: Makes project-based learning visible through evidence of practice and student learning.

title: BPI Integration
summary: Teachers plan, teach and assess BPIs; students use their criteria to evaluate and improve work.
criteria: Teachers **plan, teach and assess BRIDGE Performance Indicators (BPIs)** alongside academic standards. Students explain the BPI, **use its criteria to assess and improve work**, and show how their performance changed.
description: Accountability measure: percentage of reviewed **student BPI learning cycles** meeting the expectation below. Teachers **plan, teach and assess BRIDGE Performance Indicators (BPIs)** alongside academic standards. Students explain the BPI, **use its criteria to assess and improve work**, and show how their performance changed.
evidence: Dated student work, criteria shared before assessment, individual demonstrations, project milestones, BPI feedback, website reviews and presentation evidence. Record the district schedule for portfolios, websites and Presentations of Learning; weekly writing is measured separately.
why: Makes bpi integration visible through evidence of practice and student learning.

title: BPI Website Usage
unit: scheduled student website-review cycles in grades 3-12
summary: Grade 3-12 BPI websites contain dated, indicator-linked evidence and reflection that students can navigate and explain.
criteria: In **grades 3-12**, students maintain BPI portfolio websites with **dated, indicator-linked evidence and reflection**. They navigate their sites, explain what artifacts demonstrate and identify next steps. Teachers schedule updates and review; links work, access is supported and privacy is protected.
description: Accountability measure: percentage of reviewed **scheduled student website-review cycles in grades 3-12** meeting the expectation below. In **grades 3-12**, students maintain BPI portfolio websites with **dated, indicator-linked evidence and reflection**. They navigate their sites, explain what artifacts demonstrate and identify next steps. Teachers schedule updates and review; links work, access is supported and privacy is protected.
evidence: Dated student work, criteria shared before assessment, individual demonstrations, project milestones, BPI feedback, website reviews and presentation evidence. Record the district schedule for portfolios, websites and Presentations of Learning; weekly writing is measured separately.
why: Makes bpi website usage visible through evidence of practice and student learning.

title: Individual Learning in Collaborative Work
unit: individual student records within collaborative tasks
summary: Each student explains their contribution and demonstrates targeted learning; group completion does not establish individual mastery.
criteria: For collaborative work, teachers collect **individual explanations, demonstrations or work samples**. Each student explains their contribution and independently demonstrates the targeted learning, **with required accommodations and supports**.
description: Accountability measure: percentage of reviewed **individual student records within collaborative tasks** meeting the expectation below. For collaborative work, teachers collect **individual explanations, demonstrations or work samples**. Each student explains their contribution and independently demonstrates the targeted learning, **with required accommodations and supports**.
evidence: Dated student work, criteria shared before assessment, individual demonstrations, project milestones, BPI feedback, website reviews and presentation evidence. Record the district schedule for portfolios, websites and Presentations of Learning; weekly writing is measured separately.
why: Makes individual learning in collaborative work visible through evidence of practice and student learning.

toolTitle: Proficiency Scales in Use by Students
title: Proficiency Scales: Check Work in Progress
summary: At least once during instruction on each Priority Standard, students use its scale to check and improve unfinished work.
criteria: Teachers provide **aligned Proficiency Scales for Priority Standards**. At least once during instruction on each Priority Standard, students **use the scale to check their own unfinished work**, cite evidence, identify a next step and **act on it while time remains**. Example analysis before first demonstration is reported separately under Learning with Purpose.
description: Accountability measure: percentage of reviewed **student-standard opportunities** meeting the expectation below. Teachers provide **aligned Proficiency Scales for Priority Standards**. At least once during instruction on each Priority Standard, students **use the scale to check their own unfinished work**, cite evidence, identify a next step and **act on it while time remains**. Example analysis before first demonstration is reported separately under Learning with Purpose.
evidence: Aligned scales, annotated examples, work-in-progress checks, feedback, before/after work, reassessment and common-scoring records. Keep exemplar analysis and self-check results in their separate reporting homes.
why: Students learn to spot what their own work needs while they can still improve it.

title: Timely Feedback Aligned to Mastery
summary: Feedback identifies evidence against the standard or scale and a usable next step while learning is underway.
criteria: Teachers and peers provide **specific feedback tied to the standard or scale while there is time to use it**. Feedback identifies a feature of the work, what meets the expectation and what needs improvement. Students explain **what they will do next**.
description: Accountability measure: percentage of reviewed **student feedback opportunities** meeting the expectation below. Teachers and peers provide **specific feedback tied to the standard or scale while there is time to use it**. Feedback identifies a feature of the work, what meets the expectation and what needs improvement. Students explain **what they will do next**.
evidence: Aligned scales, annotated examples, work-in-progress checks, feedback, before/after work, reassessment and common-scoring records. Keep exemplar analysis and self-check results in their separate reporting homes.
why: Timely, specific feedback helps students know where to focus their effort before the work is finished.

title: Revision Based on Feedback
summary: Students act on feedback and explain the improvement; teachers reassess the targeted learning.
criteria: Students **revise an explanation, solution, draft or performance in response to feedback** and explain how the change better meets the criteria. Teachers provide time to act on feedback and **reassess the targeted learning** using revised work or a new demonstration.
description: Accountability measure: percentage of reviewed **student feedback-and-revision cycles** meeting the expectation below. Students **revise an explanation, solution, draft or performance in response to feedback** and explain how the change better meets the criteria. Teachers provide time to act on feedback and **reassess the targeted learning** using revised work or a new demonstration.
evidence: Aligned scales, annotated examples, work-in-progress checks, feedback, before/after work, reassessment and common-scoring records. Keep exemplar analysis and self-check results in their separate reporting homes.
why: Students see how a specific change can strengthen their reasoning, correct a misunderstanding, or improve their performance.

title: Consistent Assessment and Scoring
summary: Teacher teams independently score common work, resolve differences with criteria and check agreement again.
criteria: Teacher teams **independently score common student work with shared criteria**, compare judgments and resolve differences using evidence. They refine examples and scoring guidance, then check agreement again so that **the same quality of work receives a consistent judgment** across classrooms.
description: Accountability measure: percentage of reviewed **teacher-team scoring cycles** with documented common scoring, resolution of differences and a follow-up agreement check. Teacher teams **independently score common student work with shared criteria**, compare judgments and resolve differences using evidence. They refine examples and scoring guidance, then check agreement again so that **the same quality of work receives a consistent judgment** across classrooms.
evidence: Aligned scales, annotated examples, work-in-progress checks, feedback, before/after work, reassessment and common-scoring records. Keep exemplar analysis and self-check results in their separate reporting homes.
why: Makes consistent assessment and scoring visible through evidence of practice and student learning.

title: Timely Support and Extension
summary: Current evidence triggers targeted teaching or extension while maintaining access to challenging grade-level learning.
criteria: Teachers use **current checks of understanding** to identify specific learning needs and respond during instruction. They provide targeted teaching, scaffolds or **extension for students who already demonstrate mastery**, while maintaining access to challenging grade-level learning.
description: Accountability measure: percentage of reviewed **student support/extension opportunities** meeting the expectation below. Teachers use **current checks of understanding** to identify specific learning needs and respond during instruction. They provide targeted teaching, scaffolds or **extension for students who already demonstrate mastery**, while maintaining access to challenging grade-level learning.
evidence: Formative evidence, workshop observations, support/extension plans, tutoring schedules, attendance, parent contact, access arrangements, follow-up work and documented decisions about support.
why: Students can work through difficulty and build independence while still doing the challenging thinking themselves.

title: Student Collaboration
summary: Students contribute reasoning, respond to peers and explain how collaboration improved their understanding; participation is equitable.
criteria: Students **contribute ideas, explain reasoning, listen and build on or question peer thinking** toward a shared learning purpose. Each student explains their contribution, what they learned and **how a peer's thinking improved their understanding or work**. Teachers ensure equitable participation.
description: Accountability measure: percentage of reviewed **individual student collaboration records** meeting the expectation below. Students **contribute ideas, explain reasoning, listen and build on or question peer thinking** toward a shared learning purpose. Each student explains their contribution, what they learned and **how a peer's thinking improved their understanding or work**. Teachers ensure equitable participation.
evidence: Formative evidence, workshop observations, support/extension plans, tutoring schedules, attendance, parent contact, access arrangements, follow-up work and documented decisions about support.
why: Working with peers gives students a chance to test their ideas and improve their understanding.

title: Reflection and Next Steps
summary: Students identify patterns, set a specific goal and strategy, then check progress in the next task or unit.
criteria: Students review earlier work and feedback to identify **a pattern in strengths or learning needs**. They set a specific goal, name a strategy or support, and **check progress during the next task or unit**, adjusting their approach when needed.
description: Accountability measure: percentage of reviewed **student reflection-and-goal cycles** meeting the expectation below. Students review earlier work and feedback to identify **a pattern in strengths or learning needs**. They set a specific goal, name a strategy or support, and **check progress during the next task or unit**, adjusting their approach when needed.
evidence: Formative evidence, workshop observations, support/extension plans, tutoring schedules, attendance, parent contact, access arrangements, follow-up work and documented decisions about support.
why: Students can carry forward what worked and make a practical plan for a challenge they are likely to face again.

title: Strategic and Systematic Interventions
summary: Targeted tutoring has a provider, schedule, regular attendance, parent communication, access support and progress monitoring.
criteria: Teams identify **who needs tutoring, the learning target, provider and schedule**. Before-, during-, or after-school tutoring is available and attended regularly by identified students. **Parents are notified and encouraged to support attendance**. Staff address access barriers, monitor attendance and learning, and adjust support.
description: Accountability measure: percentage of reviewed **identified students' scheduled intervention cycles** meeting the expectation below. Teams identify **who needs tutoring, the learning target, provider and schedule**. Before-, during-, or after-school tutoring is available and attended regularly by identified students. **Parents are notified and encouraged to support attendance**. Staff address access barriers, monitor attendance and learning, and adjust support.
evidence: Formative evidence, workshop observations, support/extension plans, tutoring schedules, attendance, parent contact, access arrangements, follow-up work and documented decisions about support.
why: Makes strategic and systematic interventions visible through evidence of practice and student learning.

title: Workshop Model
summary: Workshops combine focused teaching, protected application, responsive conferences or small groups, and reflection.
criteria: Instruction includes **a focused mini-lesson or model, protected practice or application, responsive conferring or small groups, and reflection or sharing**. Teachers use formative evidence to select the teaching focus and support. Students explain their learning goal and **apply learning with increasing independence**.
description: Accountability measure: percentage of reviewed **workshop learning opportunities** meeting the expectation below. Instruction includes **a focused mini-lesson or model, protected practice or application, responsive conferring or small groups, and reflection or sharing**. Teachers use formative evidence to select the teaching focus and support. Students explain their learning goal and **apply learning with increasing independence**.
evidence: Formative evidence, workshop observations, support/extension plans, tutoring schedules, attendance, parent contact, access arrangements, follow-up work and documented decisions about support.
why: Makes workshop model visible through evidence of practice and student learning.

title: Intervention Effectiveness and Follow-up
summary: Follow-up work shows whether the targeted learning improved and informs continuation, change, intensification or conclusion of support.
criteria: Staff compare follow-up work with the **specific learning need that prompted support**. They document whether understanding, accuracy or independence improved and decide to **continue, change, intensify or conclude support**. Attendance alone does not demonstrate the intervention's effectiveness.
description: Accountability measure: percentage of reviewed **student intervention-review cycles** meeting the expectation below. Staff compare follow-up work with the **specific learning need that prompted support**. They document whether understanding, accuracy or independence improved and decide to **continue, change, intensify or conclude support**. Attendance alone does not demonstrate the intervention's effectiveness.
evidence: Formative evidence, workshop observations, support/extension plans, tutoring schedules, attendance, parent contact, access arrangements, follow-up work and documented decisions about support.
why: Makes intervention effectiveness and follow-up visible through evidence of practice and student learning.

title: Growth Across All Grades and Content Areas
unit: student learning-goal records in each grade and content area
summary: Growth is evaluated in every grade and content area using comparable earlier/later evidence and individual learning goals.
criteria: Growth is evaluated in **all grade levels and all subjects and content areas**, including and extending beyond reading and mathematics. Students and teachers compare **earlier and later evidence against the same learning expectation and criteria**. Students explain what improved and what helped. Teachers monitor **individual learning goals**, including for students already above expectations, and respond when progress is insufficient. Report separately the proportion with comparable evidence and the proportion demonstrating growth toward the documented goal; missing evidence does not establish no growth.
description: Accountability measure: percentage of reviewed **student learning-goal records in each grade and content area** with evidence of learning growth toward the documented goal. Growth is evaluated in **all grade levels and all subjects and content areas**, including and extending beyond reading and mathematics. Students and teachers compare **earlier and later evidence against the same learning expectation and criteria**. Students explain what improved and what helped. Teachers monitor **individual learning goals**, including for students already above expectations, and respond when progress is insufficient. Report separately the proportion with comparable evidence and the proportion demonstrating growth toward the documented goal; missing evidence does not establish no growth.
evidence: Comparable dated work, aligned individual assessments, next-step tasks, student goals/decisions and accessible well-being feedback. For growth, mastery, readiness and agency, include all grades and content areas and report coverage and findings by grade/content area.
why: Students and families can see how far learning has moved from the student's starting point and what deserves attention next.

title: Mastery Across All Grades and Content Areas
unit: student-standard records in each grade and content area
summary: Mastery is expected and evaluated in all grades and content areas; aligned individual evidence demonstrates expected learning.
criteria: Mastery is **expected and evaluated in all grade levels and all content areas**. Students demonstrate **the standard's expected knowledge, skills and thinking** through aligned individual evidence and required accommodations. Teachers use shared criteria and sufficient evidence for the claim; **3.0 represents expected learning where scales apply**. Effort, completion and group performance are reported separately from mastery.
description: Accountability measure: percentage of reviewed **student-standard records in each grade and content area** meeting the expectation below. Mastery is **expected and evaluated in all grade levels and all content areas**. Students demonstrate **the standard's expected knowledge, skills and thinking** through aligned individual evidence and required accommodations. Teachers use shared criteria and sufficient evidence for the claim; **3.0 represents expected learning where scales apply**. Effort, completion and group performance are reported separately from mastery.
evidence: Comparable dated work, aligned individual assessments, next-step tasks, student goals/decisions and accessible well-being feedback. For growth, mastery, readiness and agency, include all grades and content areas and report coverage and findings by grade/content area.
why: Students and families can see which essential learning students have demonstrated and where more practice or support is needed.

title: Readiness Across All Grades and Content Areas
unit: student next-step demonstrations in each grade and content area
summary: Readiness is expected and evaluated across all grades and content areas against identified next-step demands.
criteria: Readiness is **expected and evaluated in all grade levels and all content areas**. Teachers identify **the demands of the next grade, course, pathway or opportunity**. Students demonstrate the relevant knowledge, skills and independence in aligned tasks, explain their evidence and identify gaps. Teachers provide **targeted preparation and opportunities to apply learning in a new context**.
description: Accountability measure: percentage of reviewed **student next-step demonstrations in each grade and content area** meeting the expectation below. Readiness is **expected and evaluated in all grade levels and all content areas**. Teachers identify **the demands of the next grade, course, pathway or opportunity**. Students demonstrate the relevant knowledge, skills and independence in aligned tasks, explain their evidence and identify gaps. Teachers provide **targeted preparation and opportunities to apply learning in a new context**.
evidence: Comparable dated work, aligned individual assessments, next-step tasks, student goals/decisions and accessible well-being feedback. For growth, mastery, readiness and agency, include all grades and content areas and report coverage and findings by grade/content area.
why: Students and families can see how today's learning prepares students for the demands of their next step.

title: Student Agency Across All Grades and Content Areas
unit: student learning-decision cycles in each grade and content area
summary: Agency is expected and evaluated across all grades and content areas through goals, decisions, monitoring and adjustment.
criteria: Student agency is **expected and evaluated in all grade levels and all content areas**. Students use **interests, passions, aspirations, skills and talents** to set goals and shape learning decisions. They select strategies, seek support, monitor evidence and adjust their approach. Across experiences, students explain **how their decisions affected learning** and take increasing responsibility for next steps.
description: Accountability measure: percentage of reviewed **student learning-decision cycles in each grade and content area** meeting the expectation below. Student agency is **expected and evaluated in all grade levels and all content areas**. Students use **interests, passions, aspirations, skills and talents** to set goals and shape learning decisions. They select strategies, seek support, monitor evidence and adjust their approach. Across experiences, students explain **how their decisions affected learning** and take increasing responsibility for next steps.
evidence: Comparable dated work, aligned individual assessments, next-step tasks, student goals/decisions and accessible well-being feedback. For growth, mastery, readiness and agency, include all grades and content areas and report coverage and findings by grade/content area.
why: Students build the independence to make thoughtful decisions and adjust their approach when a plan needs to change.

title: Student Well-being
summary: Students experience safety, belonging and support, know a trusted adult and how to obtain help; leaders follow up.
criteria: Students experience **safety, belonging and supportive relationships**, identify a trusted adult and know how to obtain help. Leaders use student feedback, attendance and participation to identify barriers and unmet social, emotional or physical needs, **respond promptly and check whether support helped**.
description: Accountability measure: percentage of reviewed **student well-being responses** meeting the expectation below. Students experience **safety, belonging and supportive relationships**, identify a trusted adult and know how to obtain help. Leaders use student feedback, attendance and participation to identify barriers and unmet social, emotional or physical needs, **respond promptly and check whether support helped**.
evidence: Comparable dated work, aligned individual assessments, next-step tasks, student goals/decisions and accessible well-being feedback. For growth, mastery, readiness and agency, include all grades and content areas and report coverage and findings by grade/content area.
why: Feeling connected and knowing where to turn for support help students participate in school and stay engaged in learning.
